atoms.b: Prime numbers are numbers that have exactly ((one ++two three)) factors: ((0 ++1 2)) and themselves.
All numbers that have ((++more_than_two less_than_two)) factors are called composite numbers.

hint.text: Prime numbers have exactly two factors: 1 and themselves. If a number has more than 2 factors it’s a composite number.

finish.text:
Did you know? 1 is neither a prime number nor a composite.
It is only divisible by one number, itself, so it doesn’t fulfil the rules for a prime number, which needs to be divisible by exactly 2 numbers.
